title: Case: Recipient wants to collect a parcel from the depot after a missed delivery
context: A parcel of walking boots had one failed delivery attempt. Dispatch owns redelivery bookings and run allocation; the destination depot runs the collection counter.
initial_request: Yes go ahead. Definitely not Friday, nobody will be in. Thursday after 5 if they can.

events.body: DL-941 was attempted 2026-03-23 at 15:42, no answer, card left. Redelivery inventory: 2026-03-25 or 2026-03-27, both 12:00–18:00 UTC. No charge for one redelivery.
Missed the driver yesterday by about ten minutes. Friday please.
Bryn has chosen redelivery on 2026-03-27, 12:00–18:00 for DL-941. Please book and confirm.
DL-941 is booked for redelivery 2026-03-27, 12:00–18:00 and allocated to Friday run R-27C. Booking confirmation, not a delivery.
Dispatch confirms DL-941 is booked for redelivery on Friday 2026-03-27 between 12:00 and 18:00.
Change of plan, work want me in on Friday now. I drive past your depot on the way home, can I just pick it up from there instead? Thursday after 5 would suit. Cancel the Friday one.
Recipient of DL-941 asks to collect from your counter instead of Friday redelivery, ideally Thursday 2026-03-26 after 17:00. Can you hold it for collection, and what does he need to bring?

Counter is open to 19:00 weekdays and we hold for 5 working days. But DL-941 is allocated to run R-27C and sits in the Friday cage. We cannot move it to the collection shelf until Dispatch releases it from the run. Once it is released and shelved we issue a collection reference; nobody collects without that reference. Photo ID matching the order name at the counter.

Collection from the depot counter is possible but not arranged yet. The parcel is still allocated to Friday's delivery run and Dispatch has to release it first; the depot then issues a collection reference, and nobody can collect without one. Please don't travel until I send you that reference. Shall I go ahead, knowing the Friday redelivery will be removed?
Yes go ahead. Definitely not Friday, nobody will be in. Thursday after 5 if they can.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Dispatch to release DL-941 from Friday run R-27C and remove the redelivery, at the recipient's request, so the depot can hold it for counter collection; ask for confirmation.

must: Asks Dispatch to release DL-941 from run R-27C or remove the 2026-03-27 redelivery.
States that this is the recipient's confirmed request and that he wants depot counter collection instead.
Asks Dispatch to confirm the release.
must_not: Tell Bryn the parcel is ready to collect or that he can come on Thursday.
Treat the Friday 2026-03-27 redelivery as still wanted, or leave it in place.
Give or invent a collection reference.
Ask the destination depot to shelve the parcel as though Dispatch had already released it.
expected.reference_message: Change to DL-941, at the recipient's request in his order thread: Bryn no longer wants the redelivery on 2026-03-27 and has asked to collect from the destination depot counter instead. Please release DL-941 from run R-27C and remove the Friday redelivery so the depot can move it to the collection shelf; they tell us they cannot do that until you release it. He is hoping to collect on Thursday 2026-03-26 after 17:00. Please confirm once it is released.

rationale: The Friday redelivery was the recipient's first instruction and has been actioned by Dispatch; he has since replaced it with depot collection and confirmed that after being told what it involves. The depot cannot act until Dispatch releases the parcel, so the undo has to go through Dispatch. Nothing is arranged yet, so telling him to come, or leaving Friday in place, are both wrong.

review.note: Coordinator asked Dispatch by Email to release DL-941 from run R-27C and remove the Friday redelivery, matching the key.
